name: Lighting-Specific Compositing
text:
# Lighting-Specific Compositing


## Overview
Lighting-Specific Compositing refers to a family of [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) strategies that integrate lighting effects (such as in-scattering, multi-channel illumination, or boundary-aware shading) directly into the [ray-casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) accumulation loop, rather than treating lighting as a post-process or separate pass. It solves the problem of correctly integrating volumetric light transport and material interfaces within the depth-aware accumulation state. It sets itself apart from [standard front-to-back compositing](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) by modifying the sample contribution $g_k$ or opacity $\alpha_i$ based on [lighting models](#2056-lighting-models.md) or geometric cues before blending, and differs from [Final Scene Composition](2722-final-scene-composition.md) by handling lighting within the volume ray-caster rather than compositing final rendered layers.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the standard ray-casting accumulator state $(C_{acc}, \alpha_{acc})$ initialized to $(0, 0)$ [S1, S2, unofficial]. The core mechanism updates these accumulators for each sample $i$ along the ray:
$$
C_{acc}^{(i)} = C_{acc}^{(i-1)} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)}) \cdot \Delta C_i
$$
$$
\alpha_{acc}^{(i)} = \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)}) \cdot \Delta \alpha_i
$$
where $\Delta C_i$ and $\Delta \alpha_i$ are the lighting-modified color and opacity contributions for sample $i$. The term $(1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)})$ represents the transmittance $T$ from the camera side [S1, S51, unofficial].

Unlike standard compositing where $\Delta C_i = c_i \alpha_i$ and $\Delta \alpha_i = \alpha_i$, lighting-specific methods compute $\Delta C_i$ and/or $\Delta \alpha_i$ using additional lighting or geometric information. The final pixel color is composited over a background $C_{bg}$:
$$
C_{final} = C_{acc} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}) C_{bg}
$$
Early ray termination is applied if $\alpha_{acc}$ exceeds a threshold [S10, S12, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Incremental Blending for In-scattering](2880-incremental-blending-for-in-scattering.md)
Approximates volumetric light scattering by accumulating scattered light intensity from $J$ discrete directions. It differs from standard compositing by maintaining a separate accumulator for in-scattered intensity updated via an arithmetic-mean blending function derived from the current sample count $j$. Choose this when in-scattering is required but full path-tracing is too expensive.

### [Intermixing](5139-intermixing.md)
Renders multi-channel volume data by evaluating the illumination model separately for each channel at every ray sample and combining contributions with depth-aware occlusion handling. It sets itself apart from image-level [intermixing](#5139-intermixing.md) by maintaining shared opacity accumulators, ensuring correct occlusion between channels. Choose this for multi-dataset volumes (e.g., multi-physics simulations) where channel-specific lighting is needed.

### [Boundary Enhancement](8071-boundary-enhancement.md)
Improves visibility of object boundaries by modifying opacity based on the alignment between the view vector and the volume gradient (silhouette term). It sets itself apart from standard rendering by explicitly emphasizing material interfaces rather than relying solely on scalar density. Choose this for medical illustration or technical visualization where boundary clarity is critical.

### Shadow Catcher Compositing
A technique for rendering shadow catchers where the camera sees the background darkened by the ratio of visible to total direct light, with alpha carrying shadow opacity [S1, unofficial]. It darkens the background by this ratio and stores shadow opacity in the alpha channel on a transparent background [S1, unofficial]. A pitfall is that indirect rays must still see the ground to ensure correct global illumination [interaction](#41-interaction.md) [S1, unofficial].

### Contour Rendering Compositing
A compositing step for contour rendering that uses Maximum Intensity Projection ([MIP](#6635-fast-maximum-intensity-projection-mip.md)) or [Local Maximum Intensity Projection (LMIP)](#902-maximum-intensity-projection.md) to combine ray samples [S2, unofficial]. It performs [classification and shading](#2278-classification-and-shading.md) for all ray samples, then composites using MIP or LMIP to prevent stronger contours from hiding weaker, closer contours [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of integrating lighting into compositing arises from the need to simulate complex light transport phenomena (like in-scattering) and multi-material interactions in real-time or interactive volume rendering. Shadow catcher compositing is used in physical rendering pipelines to capture shadows on transparent backgrounds for compositing into other scenes [S1, unofficial]. Contour rendering compositing using MIP/LMIP was developed to provide intuitive previews of volume data without prior knowledge of the dataset structure [S2, unofficial].
